### [How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Oct/31/how-we-took-over-chatgpt-accounts/)

**Simon Willison** · 2026-10-31

Parameter Labs discovered a complex attack chain in ChatGPT that allowed full account takeover and data exfiltration via a malicious share URL.

- A sandboxed iframe used postMessage() to trigger the MathLive library's virtual keyboard on the parent page, exploiting an innerHTML vulnerability to inject an un-sandboxed iframe.
- The attack bypassed Content Security Policy (CSP) inline script restrictions by reflecting executable JavaScript through YouTube's allowed oEmbed endpoint.
- Executing arbitrary JavaScript on chatgpt.com enabled fetching private user data via API calls and exfiltrating it using image references.
- OpenAI patched the vulnerability and awarded a $5,000 bug bounty.

**Why it matters:** The exploit demonstrates how combining DOM-based XSS, iframe sandbox escapes, and CSP bypasses via trusted third-party endpoints can fully compromise user accounts and expose private chat data.
